summary: The main family names a whole or all of a set, and the verb describes making something complete or perfect. כָּלִיל can mean entire or an offering consumed wholly; other nouns name completeness or fine attire. כַּלָּה names a bride or daughter-in-law, with a matching Akkadian word, but its relation to completion is not established. The Peshitta also has the crown-family, kept here without assuming that a crown explains the other words.

senses.definition: An entire quantity or set, whose bounds are given by the following noun or the context.

evidence.note: God sees all that he has made.

senses.definition: Each member of a class; under a negative, not any member.

evidence.note: From every tree of the garden you may eat.
You shall not do any work.

senses.definition: The woman entering marriage, or addressed in bridal language.

evidence.note: A bride adorns herself with jewels.

senses.definition: The wife of someone’s son.

evidence.note: Sarai is Terah’s daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram.

words.summary: The woman in a marriage, or the wife of one’s son. The link to the root’s completion-family is unclear; the matching Akkadian word supports the family relationship rather than a derivation from “complete”.

senses.definition: Entirely of a material, or complete in the quality specified.

evidence.note: The robe is entirely of blue.
The beauty is complete through the splendor given to her.

senses.definition: An offering given wholly to the altar rather than partly eaten.

evidence.note: Every priest’s grain offering is כָּלִיל and must not be eaten.

senses.definition: Bring something to its full state; both occurrences describe completing Tyre’s beauty.

evidence.note: The builders perfected your beauty.
The shields hung on the walls complete the city’s beauty.

senses.definition: The impressive equipment or clothing in which troops are arrayed.

evidence.note: Assyrian warriors are clothed in מִכְלוֹל.

words.summary: Both occurrences describe military dress. The context supports splendid or complete attire; the noun’s exact range is limited by these two uses.

senses.definition: Goods of fine clothing or textiles in Tyre’s trade; attested only here in the plural.

evidence.note: Listed with blue and embroidered fabrics among the traded wares.

senses.definition: The complete or perfect expression of a quality; in its single occurrence, Zion’s beauty.

evidence.note: Zion is the perfection of beauty.

senses.definition: The time or state of being a bride, in the image of Israel’s early devotion.

evidence.note: The love of your כְּלוּלֹת is parallel to the devotion of your youth.

words.summary: Attested only in a plural expression for Israel’s bridal time or state. Its link is to the bride-word; a more precise distinction between betrothal and marriage is not fixed by this verse alone.

senses.definition: A whole set, or each member of it.

evidence.note: The king is made ruler over them all.
The kingdom devours the whole earth.

senses.definition: Bring construction to completion.

evidence.note: The king built and completed the house.

senses.definition: Of walls whose building is finished.

evidence.note: If the city is rebuilt and its walls completed.

senses.definition: The whole of something or every member of a stated class.

evidence.note: All the generations are counted in three groups.

senses.definition: The woman joined to a bridegroom, also used in the image of the holy city.

evidence.note: The one who has the bride is the bridegroom.

senses.definition: A son’s wife, set in relation to her mother-in-law.

evidence.note: Daughter-in-law and mother-in-law are set against one another.

senses.definition: A head-wreath, including the crown of thorns.

evidence.note: They weave thorns into a crown and place it on his head.

senses.definition: A crown promised or awarded, or a person spoken of as someone’s crown.

evidence.note: Athletes compete for a perishable crown; believers for an imperishable one.

words.summary: A circlet or wreath worn on the head, and figuratively a reward or honor. The relation of crowning to the other כלל meanings is not established by the cited verses.

senses.definition: Receive the athlete’s crown; this word occurs only here in the Peshitta.

evidence.note: An athlete is not crowned unless he competes lawfully.

cognates.note: The noun’s constructions express a whole or any member; the adjective kulliyy means total or universal.

note: The bride and completion words are retained together without an asserted etymology. The crown-family is included from scripture’s Syriac, whose root key is כל. כְּלָל is a person’s name, left for its own entry; the remaining unassigned BDB rows are redirects. xk.ad.ab and k.bn.ab overlap on Hebrew spellings, and support counts cannot be read as separate language totals. The brief for כלל omits the Aramaic quantifier because it is filed under כל; that word is included here. Cognate assignment deliberately separates the bridal and totality senses, so a negative evidence balance is expected for each group rather than concealed.
